messages:
sam: heads-up — us-west2 batch pool is noisy, DCGM exporter fired ~20 ECC uncorrectable alerts in 12m for card0 on node i-0a12bf. Alerts are flapping, causing automated drain churn :grimacing:

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2025-483. Auto-drain triggered for node i-0a12bf after 3 alerts in 10m.

maria: saw that — looks like a burst pattern (short spikes on a single card). Not a hardware death but noisy errors. Drains are expensive and causing job retries.

jonathan: quick data — over last 2h topology: 1 node, card0 24 spikes (mostly 1-2x increases), other cards quiet. No Xid stream, just ECC uncorrected counters.

lee: proposal: deglitch the alerting and only escalate when errors are sustained across windows or spread across MIG contexts. Right now the rule is:

```yaml
alert: GPU_ECC_Uncorrected
expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_uncorrectable_total[5m]) > 0
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
```

lee: that fires on any 1 spike in 5m and then autoscaler/drain kicks in. I suggest switching to a two-part rule: a noisy suppression recording rule and an escalation alert that requires either (a) sustained increase over 15m OR (b) concurrent increases on >1 MIG-context/card on the same host.

sam: SGTM. Can you sketch the PromQL for the escalation?

lee: something like —

```promql
# recording: per-card 5m increase
record: job:gpu:ecc_increase:5m
expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_uncorrectable_total{job=\"dcgm\"}[5m])

# alert: sustained or multi-card
expr: (
  job:gpu:ecc_increase:5m > 0 and
  increase(job:gpu:ecc_increase:5m[3]) > 2
) or (
  count by (instance) (job:gpu:ecc_increase:5m > 0) > 1
)
for: 15m
```

maria: minor nit — use rate() for noisy counters and guard against resets. Also add a label to ignore transient maintenance windows and scheduled MIG moves.

jonathan: also add a stretch rule for sample-rate tuning: only evaluate exporter metrics at 30s scrape in hotspots, but increase evaluation range to avoid false positives. That helped with PCI bus storms in the past.

sam: ops/process question — if we change to for:15m will we miss an actual failing card that goes bad quickly? We want to avoid taking bad hardware out late.

lee: tradeoff: aggressive small-window drains cause churn and cost. Plan: use two-tier workflow — new rule with for:15m -> warn channel + add node to soft-quarantine (no immediate drain). If warnings persist or spread to other cards, escalate to hard drain. Update oncall playbook to require manual confirm for hard drains when only single-card warnings.

maria: rollout plan: 1) push recording rule first (no alerts) for 24h to gather telemetry. 2) add the new escalation alert in staging ns and run for 48h in shadow mode (page -> slack only). 3) flip to oncall paging and enable soft-quarantine automation. 4) after 7d, consider raising threshold or adding an ML filter to classify bursts vs wearout.

jonathan: I'll open a prom PR with the rules and a small grafana panel for per-card spike density. Also add a short runbook snippet:

```
Runbook: GPU ECC spike warning
- If single-card warning: tag node soft-quarantine, avoid auto-drain.
- Check DCGM logs: dcgm_smi, dmesg, nvidia-smi -q.
- If Xid errors or repeated increases across cards: escalate to drain + RMA.
- If suspected noise (one-off <2 spikes/hour): clear and monitor 24h.
```

sam: thanks — good balance. Can we also log the cost impact of drains in the PR? e.g., avg job retries and lost GPU-hours per drain. Helps eng leadership.

lee: yes, will include a quick cost table and tie the change to a conservative SLO for detection latency.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled maint in us-west2 at 2025-06-16T02:00Z — exclude that window from escalation rules.

maria: awesome. i'll coordinate the shadow run and watch the slack channel for warnings.

sam: thanks team — target to merge PR + start shadow by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
